sections.html:
Johnston is a Polk County city on the northwest side of the Des Moines metro area. Interstate 80 forms its southern border, the Des Moines River marks the east, and the western limits run to about a half mile east of Iowa Highway 141. Downtown Des Moines is roughly 10.5 miles away, and DART buses serve the city on routes 5 and 93.

The city grew from 8,649 residents in 2000 to 24,064 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 25,065. It has 9,194 households and a median age of 37.0, and ranks 24th in Iowa by population. Such fast growth means many Johnston houses are newer than those in older Iowa cities, and a seller often competes with new construction and nearby suburbs like Urbandale and Grimes for the same buyer.

Camp Dodge, the Iowa National Guard headquarters, sits inside the city, and Johnston also holds corporate and state offices. For a seller, the takeaway is steady local demand for housing from people who work nearby.

The Johnston Community School District serves the city and parts of Des Moines, Granger, Grimes and Urbandale. It covers about 40 square miles in Polk County and enrolls 7,487 students. Schools include Johnston High School, Johnston Middle School, Summit Middle School and elementary schools named Beaver Creek, Horizon, Lawson, Timber Ridge and Wallace, plus an early learning academy for preschool.

The city has 12 parks and more than 45 miles of trails. Terra Park covers 200 acres and has an amphitheater, a community center, a playground and a fishing pier. The Beaver Creek Access Point, near 86th Street and 70th Avenue, is on the Iowa Confluence Water Trails and offers kayak rentals, and Johnston Town Center has an events space called The Yard, shops and an outdoor synthetic ice rink.

If your house is close to a trailhead or park, say so when you describe it to a buyer.

Saylorville Lake is a flood control reservoir on the Des Moines River about 11 miles upstream from Des Moines, run by the Army Corps of Engineers, Rock Island District. At normal pool it covers about 5,950 acres, and at full flood pool it can reach 16,700 acres. The reservoir hit its record level of 892.03 feet on July 11, 1993.

A house near the river or Beaver Creek should be checked against flood maps before you list. Ask the insurer, ask the city and keep any flood claim records handy, since buyers often request them.

Johnston City Hall is at 6221 Merle Hay Road, phone 515-278-2344. The city's website links to permits for accessory buildings, decks and pools, and separate forms cover right-of-way work. Utility start, stop and transfer requests go through the city, and trash and recycling pickup is handled through the MWA collection service.

If you added a deck, shed or pool without checking permits, sort that out before a buyer's inspector notices. An open or missing permit can stall a loan-based sale, while a cash buyer simply factors it into the offer.

Polk County bills the tax, and the Polk County Treasurer answers at 515-286-3060.

InstallmentDueLate interest starts
First halfSeptember 1October 1, at 1.5 percent a month
Second halfMarch 1April 1, at 1.5 percent a month

Taxes are usually prorated at closing, and the buyer gets a credit or the seller pays the treasurer. Iowa also applies a transfer tax of eighty cents per $500 of value above the first $500 on deeds with consideration (Iowa Code 428A.1). Assessments are updated every other year, and owners can protest to the Board of Review from April 2 through April 30.

Polk County sells unpaid taxes at an annual online tax sale, held each June, and the buyer receives a lien on the property. An owner can pay before the cutoff the day before the sale to avoid it.

After a tax sale, redemption costs the full delinquent amount plus 2 percent per month, and partial payments are not allowed. If a lien is not redeemed in the time Iowa law sets, the certificate holder can start a tax deed proceeding. A notice to redeem should prompt a call to the treasurer right away.

  • Pay delinquent tax before the sale if you can.
  • Do not count on a mailed redemption. It must arrive by the last day of the month, and the postmark does not count.
  • Tell any buyer about a tax sale lien in writing.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Johnston house?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Johnston follows the same steps as any other Iowa sale, minus the mortgage. You describe the house, a buyer makes a written offer, and a title company handles the closing paperwork.

  1. Describe the house, including repairs, permits and anything owed.
  2. Review the written offer and decide.
  3. If you accept, the title company runs the search and prepares the deed.
  4. At closing, taxes and any liens are paid from the proceeds.

That route suits owners who are moving for a new job, selling an inherited house or dealing with repairs they would rather not manage. You can say no and owe nothing.

A Johnston sale goes smoothly when the paperwork is ready. Collect the deed and any survey, the latest Polk County tax statement, permit records for decks, sheds and pools, and any flood claim or repair receipts. If someone rents the house, add the lease and agree on a move-out date in writing.

Two calls help. Phone the Polk County Treasurer at 515-286-3060 to confirm both installments are paid or to learn what is owed. Then contact the city at 515-278-2344 to schedule utility stop and transfer service for the closing date, so the buyer is not billed for your last weeks.

Finally, think about what you are leaving behind. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, but furniture, trash and stored items still need a plan. Decide what goes with you, what is donated and what is left for the buyer, and say so before the offer is final.

sections.h2: Moving fast or inheriting a house
sections.html:
Johnston draws people for jobs in the metro, and some of them leave just as quickly. If you are relocating and the house is still yours, the timeline matters more than the last few thousand dollars of price. A listing means showings, an appraisal and a buyer's financing, any of which can slip. A cash sale lets you pick the closing date within what the title work allows.

With an inherited house, start by confirming whose names are on the deed and whether anything is owed in taxes or liens. The title company can only close once the right people sign, so getting that straight first saves weeks. A house that sat empty may also need a walk-through for water or heating problems, and a cash buyer will price those in.

faqs.a: Johnston is in Polk County in the Des Moines metro area, with I-80 on its southern edge and the Des Moines River on its eastern edge. It is about 10.5 miles from downtown Des Moines.

faqs.q: How many people live in Johnston?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 24,064 residents, up from 8,649 in 2000. The 2025 estimate is 25,065.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Johnston?
faqs.a: The Polk County Treasurer bills it. Payments are due September 1 and March 1, and interest starts the first of the following month.
The Johnston Community School District, which covers about 40 square miles and enrolls 7,487 students. It also serves parts of Des Moines, Granger, Grimes and Urbandale.
Parts of the city are near the Des Moines River, Beaver Creek and Saylorville Reservoir. Check your parcel with the city and your insurer.
